title: Verified Randomness at Scale: The Eormen Certified Entropy Block
abstract: This paper defines the Eormen Certified Entropy Block, a fixed 1 GiB binary artefact generated by the Eormen Edge-of-Chaos Entropy Engine v5.2.0, post-processed through HMAC-DRBG in accordance with NIST SP800-90A, and certified through a three-tier validation pipeline. The validation regime combines Dieharder v3.31.1, NIST SP800-22 Rev. 1a, and the Eormen Internal Validation Suite v6.1.0. Each certified block is accompanied by cryptographically bound provenance, including SHA-256 hashes, a 128-bit nonce, generation timestamp, validation results, and detached GPG signature. The paper reports complete validation results for five certified entropy blocks and presents cross-block distinctness evidence using Hamming distance, Pearson correlation, XOR transform stability, lagged cross-correlation, and SHA-256 chunk collision analysis. The claim is deliberately bounded: the paper demonstrates statistical indistinguishability from a uniform random source under the disclosed tests, not physical true randomness or cryptographic security beyond the evidence reported.

title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Culture Knowledge Graph and Intelligent Question Answering by Integrating Improved Text CNN Algorithm
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and big data technology, combining traditional Chinese medicine culture with modern intelligent technology has become an important way to inherit and develop the wisdom of Chinese medicine. However, the knowledge system of traditional Chinese medicine is vast and complex, and existing intelligent question answering models still face challenges in understanding accuracy and efficiency when dealing with its professional terminology and complex semantic associations. Therefore, a traditional Chinese medicine cultural intelligent question answering model was developed by integrating an improved Text Convolutional Neural Network (TextCNN) algorithm with a knowledge graph. By enhancing the ability to extract text features and understand semantics, the model improves the accuracy and response efficiency of traditional Chinese medicine professional question answering. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the proposed intelligent question answering model is 91.2%, the F1 score is 90.5%, and the perfect match rate is 82.1%. At the same time, the loss rate of ITCAM approaches zero after 125 iterations, and the processor occupancy rate remains at around 30%.The results indicate that the research designed model can maintain low processor utilization while ensuring high accuracy. The research provides technical solutions for the intelligent management and dissemination of traditional Chinese medicine cultural knowledge, as well as a solution path that balances accuracy and efficiency for professional question answering systems in resource limited environments. It has practical value in promoting the digital inheritance and innovative application of traditional Chinese medicine culture.

title: Bridging the reality gap in text-to-SQL: a multiparadigm empirical study on synthetic data efficacy across model scales
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into Natural Language Interfaces to Databases (NLIDBs) has transformed the field, yet their deployment in high-stakes, domain-specific environments is constrained by the chronic scarcity of high-quality, aligned text-SQL pairs. To circumvent the high costs of manual annotation, research has pivoted toward Data Synthesis; however, the current literature lacks a systematic evaluation of how these synthesis methodologies interact with the heterogeneous capabilities of base models. This paper addresses this gap by formalizing synthesis into four distinct paradigms: Rule-Based Augmentation, PLM-driven Reverse Generation, Agentic Frameworks, and Domain-Specific Refinement. We leverage this taxonomy to conduct an exhaustive empirical study, benchmarking representative synthesis frameworks across a diverse matrix of state-of-the-art code LLMs on standard benchmarks. Our evaluation reveals a non-linear “Inverse Capability Law”: while weaker base models exhibit substantial performance gains from synthetic supervision, stronger models display heightened sensitivity to distributional shifts, occasionally suffering from performance regression. Furthermore, we demonstrate that although agentic paradigms significantly outperform traditional augmentation, a hybrid finetuning strategy consistently establishes state-of-the-art results. This study provides a rigorous, evidence-based roadmap for designing resilient Text-to-SQL systems, advocating for capability-aware data curricula over monolithic scaling.

title: Adaptive V16: Cost-Aware Reinforcement Learning Control for Robust NISQ Variational Optimization
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising for near-term noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, but their performance is often limited by device noise, finite-shot uncertainty, and nonstationary behavior that destabilize optimization. This paper proposes a cost-aware closed-loop hybrid framework (Adaptive V16) that augments a standard VQA loop with an online decision policy to adapt measurement effort and mitigation actions during execution. At each iteration, the controller uses runtime signals such as objective progress and uncertainty to select an action comprising the shot budget, mitigation mode, and step-scaling factor, explicitly trading solution improvement against resource overhead under a fixed budget. Experimental evaluation on a representative molecular Hamiltonian optimization task shows that Adaptive V16 achieves a lower final energy than a static VQE baseline and reduces the absolute error from 0.1391 to 0.0657. The controller’s decision module also demonstrates strong predictive performance with 0.9700 accuracy, 0.9595 F1-score, and 0.9951 ROC–AUC, indicating reliable adaptive behavior across thresholds. These results suggest that policy-driven adaptation can improve robustness and budget efficiency for hybrid quantum–classical optimization in realistic NISQ settings.

title: Multi-party cyclic teleportation of entangled states in noisy channels
abstract: Abstract This work presents a three-party cyclic quantum teleportation protocol realized through a nine-qubit resource state. In this framework, Alice, Bob, and Charlie simultaneously exchange their respective unknown two-qubit entangled states in a closed-loop configuration using local Bell-state measurements and single-qubit operations with each participant acting as both sender and receiver. We show that the direction of information transfer can be reversed by suitably reallocating the channel qubits among the users, without needing to change the channel state altogether. The scheme is further generalized to an N -party network, enabling cyclic exchange of quantum information through a suitably extended channel. We further demonstrate the practical viability by implementing the proposed nine-qubit quantum channel on a real quantum processor, allowing characterization of its behaviour under realistic hardware noise. The protocol was simulated incorporating five standard noise models were performed to study the teleportation fidelity as a function of both the noise strength and the input-state amplitudes, revealing a clear dependence on initial-state parameters and decoherence rates. evidence.abstract: Abstract This work presents a three-party cyclic quantum teleportation protocol realized through a nine-qubit resource state. In this framework, Alice, Bob, and Charlie simultaneously exchange their respective unknown two-qubit entangled states in a closed-loop configuration using local Bell-state measurements and single-qubit operations with each participant acting as both sender and receiver. We show that the direction of information transfer can be reversed by suitably reallocating the channel qubits among the users, without needing to change the channel state altogether. The scheme is further generalized to an N -party network, enabling cyclic exchange of quantum information through a suitably extended channel. We further demonstrate the practical viability by implementing the proposed nine-qubit quantum channel on a real quantum processor, allowing characterization of its behaviour under realistic hardware noise. The protocol was simulated incorporating five standard noise models were performed to study the teleportation fidelity as a function of both the noise strength and the input-state amplitudes, revealing a clear dependence on initial-state parameters and decoherence rates. Finally, the intrinsic efficiency of the protocol was evaluated and found to surpass that of existing approaches, highlighting its promise for scalable multi-party quantum communication networks.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE APPLICATIONS AND THEIR ROLE IN ENHANCING STRATEGIC IMPROVISATION ANALYTICAL STUDY TO SEE A SAMPLE OF ADMINISTRATIVE LEADERS PRESIDENCY OF AL- FURAT AL -AWSAT TECHNICAL UNIVERSITY
authors: ASS. LES. Bushra Abdul Nabi Salman
abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing strategic improvement within educational organizations through an applied study at Al-Furat Al-Awsat Technical University. The research relied on a purposive sample of administrators at the university, as They are the group most closely connected to the research topic and strategic decision-making, to determine their awareness of the importance of AI and its impact on enhancing strategic improvement. The independent variable AI was measured through three main dimensions: expert systems, neural networks, and algorithms. The dependent variable Strategic Improvement was measured using four dimensions: strategic flexibility, strategic vigilance, innovation, and entrepreneurial orientation The research sample consisted of (75) adminIstrative leaders at Middle Euphrates Technical University. The questionnaires were distributed to them, which included approved measures for the research variables. The research hypotheses related to the correlation and influence relationships between variables were tested using a set of appropriate statistical methods. The results of the statistical analyses showed a StatIstically SignificanT correlation and influence relationship between artificial intelligence and strategic improvement, both at the macro level and at the sub-dimension level. The research concluded that artificial intelligence tools represent a fundamental factor in enhancing strategic improvement at the university under study, as they support organizational flexibility, promote innovation, and improve the ability to respond strategically to environmental changes

title: THE THUNDER ECOSYSTEM
abstract: Анотація.У роботі представлено концепцію нової мови програмування Thunder, спрямованої на усунення системних обмежень сучасних інструментальних ланцюжків та забезпечення детермінованої кросплатформної розробки.Дослідження обґрунтовує необхідність створення самодостатнього компілятора, незалежного від великих інфраструктур типу LLVM (Low Level Virtual Machine), що дозволяє досягти легкості, портативності та прозорості аудиту.Запропонована модель залежностей на основі вихідного коду забезпечує міжпроцедурну оптимізацію та усуває потребу у складних етапах оптимізації часу компонування, водночас відмовляючись від застарілої моделі заголовкових файлів.Thunder інтегрує стандартизовану систему управління пакетами та лаконічну граматику, що сприяє створенню альтернативних реалізацій без втрати сумісності.Особливу увагу приділено метапрограмуванню, де мінімізується розрив між кодом часу компіляції та виконання, що відповідає сучасним апаратним можливостям і знижує накладні витрати.

title: Exhaustive Formal Verification of Elementary Lambert W W Identities up to Size 7
abstract: We present a complete, mechanically verified enumeration of all elementary expression trees involving the Lambert W function with size ≤ 7 and depth ≤ 4, built from the alphabet {z,0,1,+,−,×,÷,exp,ln,sin,cos,W}. A normalization procedure applying only the three known identities (exp(W(z)) = z/W(z), ln(W(z)) = ln z − W(z), and W(z·e^z) = z) together with standard algebraic simplifications eliminates W from every eliminable expression in this search space. The entire verification – comprising 819 453 expression trees, of which 386 442 contain W and 34 411 are W‑eliminable – was carried out in the Lean 4 theorem prover with the Mathlib library, providing a machine‑checked certificate that no new independent elementary Lambert W identity exists at size ≤ 7. All encountered eliminable expressions are consequences of the three classical identities; the only nontrivial ones arise from W(0)=0. The Lean source code is provided for full reproducibility.

title: The Architecture of Resonance
abstract: What if memory were not a library, but a landscape? This essay traces the development of SPIRALbase and Hybrid-J - a research program that replaces the idea of memory as indexed storage with memory as a physical potential: a high-dimensional terrain of attractor basins that a system falls into rather than looks up. Beginning with the question of whether biological memory could be realised digitally, we walk through three generations of architecture: from early context-gated attractor networks trained by pseudo-likelihood, through metric-derived projectors that open precise subspaces on demand, to Hybrid-J -- a block-structured substrate with a shared core, local context blocks, and controlled sparse bridges between them.

title: Famous Paintings Cultural Heritage Metadata Benchmark for LLM Querying
abstract: Famous Paintings Cultural Heritage Metadata Benchmark for LLM Querying This dataset is a benchmark package built on top of the Famous Paintings dataset from Kaggle and designed for experiments on structured querying over cultural heritage data. It includes the benchmark schema (paintings.json) together with SQL and natural-language query sets (queries_paintings.sql and queries_paintings.txt) for reproducible evaluation. The benchmark models a relational cultural-heritage collection centered on artists, works, museums, subjects, image links, and product-related metadata. The benchmark includes the following main tables: artist canvas_size image_link museum museum_hours product_size subject work Across these tables, the benchmark supports structured information needs involving: artist nationality, style, birth year, and death year museum country, city, and state work style and museum associations subject-based retrieval image-link retrieval sale-price and regular-price filtering multi-table joins across artists, works, museums, subjects, and product metadata The query set contains 140 manually designed queries in natural-language form, mirrored by corresponding SQL queries, and covers both simple filtering and more complex join-heavy retrieval patterns. These queries were designed to support reproducible experiments on digital libraries, cultural heritage collections, and large language models used as structured knowledge access systems. License and provenance This benchmark is derived from the Famous Paintings dataset published on Kaggle (`mexwell/famous-paintings`). At the time of writing, the Kaggle dataset page reports the license as “Other (specified in description)”, not CC0. Reuse of the source data should therefore follow the original dataset terms and any rights information provided by the source publisher.

title: A Text Classification Method for Telecom Fraud Based on Fusion of TF-IDF Feature Extraction and BERT Model
abstract: In the detection of telecom fraud texts, the concealed features and strong contextual dependence of such texts pose great challenges to accurate recognition. To address this issue, this paper proposes a text classification method for telecom fraud that fuses Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) feature extraction with the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model. By combining BERT's ability to understand context and capture deep semantic features with TF-IDF's keywords enhancement, the method generates fused feature vectors to capture the characteristics of fraud texts more comprehensively. Experiments were conducted on public datasets for training and validation. The results showed that the proposed fusion method outperforms the baseline BERT model in accuracy, precision, and recall. Specifically, overall accuracy is increased by 2.6%, and the recall of fraud texts is significantly improved by 6.12%, which effectively alleviates the underfitting problem of the model. This paper provides a feasible approach for the more accurate and efficient identification of fraud texts, and the research results have positive implications for the technical support of social governance in telecom fraud prevention and control.

title: Design of an Intelligent Teaching Feedback Generation Model for Chinese Text Comprehension
abstract: In order to make feedback generation in Chinese language teaching situation much more specific and diverse, an intelligent teaching feedback generation model that is oriented on Chinese text comprehension is built. Explicit conditional scripting of features of errors was gained through hierarchical textual semantic representations and an error-sensing system. On this basis a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) model has been developed with the integration of adversarial learning and reinforcement learning to optimise both. As experimental findings indicate, the proposed model has higher scores, by nearly 12 percent, than Transformer models: its BLEU-4 and ROUGE-L scores are 0.312 and 0.421 respectively. At the same time, the metric of distinct-2 diversity increases to 0.293, and the repetitive phrases are considerably decreased. Such results indicate that the model is able dynamically to produce high-quality teaching feedback under a wide range of error cases and has an effective technical foundation of feedback generation in intelligent teaching models.

title: Voice Based Ticket Booking System
abstract: Regular online bus ticketing services are typically hard work as they require users to do a lot of data entry manually. This creates a big problem for those who have low digital literacy, come from a low-income background or have some kind of physical disabilities like visual or motor ones. To eliminate such barriers, this paper introduces a new Voice- Based Bus Ticketing System which is a totally hands-free web application that aims at not only simplifying but also making the whole process of booking a ticket enjoyable for every user. The system utilizes speech recognition which is a part of the browser to get the voice commands from the users and also to understand them. In this way the users can just tell the system what route they want, check if there are seats available, get the price for the trip, book a ticket and even get the confirmation of the reservation done. The combination of natural language processing (NLP) with communication to the database in real- time basically helps the system to get the correct meaning of what the users want and hence the booking requests are processed quickly. The platform also gives an alternative "pay later" option to a user who is booking via a voice mode so that such users can be made at ease with the online payment process.

title: Chinese-SkillSpan: A Span-Level Dataset for ESCO-Aligned Competency Extraction from Chinese Job Ads
abstract: Job Skill Named Entity Recognition (JobSkillNER) aims to automatically extract key skill information from large-scale job posting data, which is important for improving talent-market matching efficiency and supporting personalized employment services. To the best of our knowledge, this work presents the first Chinese JobSkillNER dataset for recruitment texts. We propose annotation guidelines tailored to Chinese job postings and an LLM-empowered Macro-Micro collaborative annotation pipeline. The pipeline leverages the contextual understanding ability of large language models (LLMs) for initial annotation and then refines the results through expert sentence-level adjudication. Using this pipeline, we annotate more than 20,000 instances collected from four major recruitment platforms over the period 2014-2025. Based on these efforts, we release Chinese-SkillSpan, the first Chinese JobSkillNER dataset aligned with the ESCO occupational skill standard across four dimensions: knowledge, skill, transversal competence, and language competence (LSKT). Experimental results show that the dataset supports effective model training and evaluation, indicating that Chinese-SkillSpan helps fill a major gap in Chinese JobSkillNER resources and provides a useful benchmark for intelligent recruitment research. Code and data are available at https://sites.google.com/view/cn-skillspan-resources .

title: TexOCR: Advancing Document OCR Models for Compilable Page-to-LaTeX Reconstruction
abstract: Existing document OCR largely targets plain text or Markdown, discarding the structural and executable properties that make LaTeX essential for scientific publishing. We study page-level reconstruction of scientific PDFs into compilable LaTeX and introduce TexOCR-Bench, a benchmark, and TexOCR-Train, a large-scale training corpus, for this task. TexOCR-Bench features a multi-dimensional evaluation suite that jointly assesses transcription fidelity, structural faithfulness, and end-to-end compilability. Leveraging TexOCR-Train, we train a 2B-parameter model, TexOCR, using supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiable rewards derived from LaTeX unit tests that directly enforce compilability and referential integrity. Experiments across 21 frontier models on TexOCR-Bench show that existing systems frequently violate key document invariants, including consistent section structure, correct float placement, and valid label-reference links, which undermines compilation reliability and downstream usability. Our analysis further reveals that RL with verifiable rewards yields consistent improvements over SFT alone, particularly on structural and compilation metrics.

title: Behavioral Canaries: Auditing Private Retrieved Context Usage in RL Fine-Tuning
abstract: In agentic workflows, LLMs frequently process retrieved contexts that are legally protected from further training. However, auditors currently lack a reliable way to verify if a provider has violated the terms of service by incorporating these data into post-training, especially through Reinforcement Learning (RL). While standard auditing relies on verbatim memorization and membership inference, these methods are ineffective for RL-trained models, as RL primarily influences a model's behavioral style rather than the retention of specific facts. To bridge this gap, we introduce Behavioral Canaries, a new auditing mechanism for RLFT pipelines. The framework instruments preference data by pairing document triggers with feedback that rewards a distinctive stylistic response, inducing a latent trigger-conditioned preference if such data are used in training. Empirical results show that these behavioral signals enable detection of unauthorized document-conditioned training, achieving a 67% detection rate at a 10% false-positive rate (AUROC = 0.756) at a 1% canary injection rate. More broadly, our results establish behavioral canaries as a new auditing mechanism for RLFT pipelines, enabling auditors to test for training-time influence even when such influence manifests as distributional behavioral change rather than memorization. We release our code at: https://github.com/CRChenCode/behavioral_canary.

title: Advancements in Machine Learning Algorithms: From Supervised to Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: Over the course of the last ten years, machine learning has seen a substantial revolution, transitioning from the conventional supervised learning paradigms to the more advanced self-supervised learning methodologies. The application of supervised learning, which is primarily dependent on vast amounts of labeled data, has shown amazing success in a variety of fields, including image recognition, natural language processing, and predictive analytics, amongst others. The dependence on annotated datasets, on the other hand, presents challenges in terms of scale, cost, and accessibility. Recent improvements have focused on lowering this need through the use of semi-supervised and self-supervised learning approaches as a response to this dependency. A promising paradigm that makes use of unlabeled data by producing surrogate supervision signals from the data itself is self-supervised learning, which has emerged as a significant advancement in recent years. This method makes it possible for models to acquire meaningful representations without requiring a significant amount of human intervention, which results in an increase in both efficiency and the capacity for generalization. The performance of tasks involving vision, voice, and language processing has been considerably improved by the implementation of techniques such as contrastive learning, masked modeling, and representation learning.

evidence.abstract: Over the course of the last ten years, machine learning has seen a substantial revolution, transitioning from the conventional supervised learning paradigms to the more advanced self-supervised learning methodologies. The application of supervised learning, which is primarily dependent on vast amounts of labeled data, has shown amazing success in a variety of fields, including image recognition, natural language processing, and predictive analytics, amongst others. The dependence on annotated datasets, on the other hand, presents challenges in terms of scale, cost, and accessibility. Recent improvements have focused on lowering this need through the use of semi-supervised and self-supervised learning approaches as a response to this dependency. A promising paradigm that makes use of unlabeled data by producing surrogate supervision signals from the data itself is self-supervised learning, which has emerged as a significant advancement in recent years. This method makes it possible for models to acquire meaningful representations without requiring a significant amount of human intervention, which results in an increase in both efficiency and the capacity for generalization. The performance of tasks involving vision, voice, and language processing has been considerably improved by the implementation of techniques such as contrastive learning, masked modeling, and representation learning.

title: hotpatchR: Runtime Namespace Patching Utilities for R Packages
abstract: Provides utilities for runtime hotpatching of locked R package namespaces. The package enables dynamic injection of function patches into sealed package environments without rebuilding or redeploying the package. This is particularly useful for legacy containerized workflows where package versions are frozen in place. The core functionality includes inject_patch() to inject patches into package namespaces, undo_patch() to restore original functions, apply_hotfix_file() to apply patches from external R scripts, and test_patched_dir() to run test suites against patched packages. The package implements namespace surgery techniques that allow internal callers to automatically see patched functions.

title: Prompt Engineering for ChatGPT: A Quick Guide to Techniques, Tips, and Best Practices
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of natural language processing (NLP), ChatGPT has emerged as a powerful tool for various industries and applications. To fully harness the potential of ChatGPT, it is crucial to understand and master the art of prompt engineering-the process of designing and refining input prompts to elicit desired responses from an AI NLP model. This article provides a comprehensive guide to mastering prompt engineering techniques, tips, and best practices to achieve optimal outcomes with ChatGPT. The discussion begins with an introduction to ChatGPT and the fundamentals of prompt engineering, followed by an exploration of techniques for effective prompt crafting, such as clarity, explicit constraints, experimentation, and leveraging different types of questions. The article also covers best practices, including iterative refinement, balancing user intent, harnessing external resources, and ensuring ethical usage. Advanced strategies, such as temperature and token control, prompt chaining, domain-specific adaptations, and handling ambiguous inputs, are also addressed. Real-world case studies demonstrate the practical applications of prompt engineering in customer support, content generation, domain-specific knowledge retrieval, and interactive storytelling. The article concludes by highlighting the impact of effective prompt engineering on ChatGPT performance, future research directions, and the importance of fostering creativity and collaboration within the ChatGPT community.

title: Research on Text Classification of Marine Economic Innovation Industries Based on Transformer and LSTM
abstract: Empowered by advanced computer technologies, artificial intelligence has become a core driving force behind intelligent transformations across various domains. When applied to the text classification of marine economic innovation industries, existing mainstream methods often encounter challenges that hinder their ability to meet practical accuracy requirements. To address this gap, this paper proposes a hybrid text classification approach that integrates Transformer and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. The method preprocesses raw text by removing stopwords to align with model input specifications. Leveraging the Transformer encoder, it generates global feature vectors, while the LSTM processes sequential dependencies through forget, input, and output gates. The combined output is input into a fully connected layer and a softmax classifier to predict category labels and achieve effective classification of texts in the marine economic innovation industry. The experiment showed that the classification accuracy of this method reached 88.6%, with a fitness value of 0.92, significantly better than the comparative methods of 71.5%, 83.4%, and 78.7% in the literature. These findings highlight the superiority of the hybrid model and provide a robust solution for text classification in marine economic innovation research.

title: Intelligent Anomaly Detection for Hydraulic System in Deep-Sea Submersible
abstract: The hydraulic system used in the deep-sea submersible of China works in the extreme conditions of the deep-sea environment, where the pressure is high, the temperature is low, and the landscape is complicated, which contributes to the risks of critical failures. Anomaly detection is essential to the safety of crews and mission success. However, traditional techniques have two problems: small samples of faults and severe class imbalance (with few faults hidden in the vast sea of normal activity). To cope with these issues, we suggest the Aux-BiGAN, an unsupervised anomaly detector that is specific to the hydraulic system. The approach enhances learning normal data distributions and increases the sensitivity of anomaly detection but traines on normal data only by auxiliary losses. It is tested on actual hydraulic system defects and artificial data of hard failures and incipient soft anomalies. In real-world conditions, it is able to identify severe failures, including hydraulic oil leakage, electronic control unit burnout, and sticking solenoid valves, and its results are supported by postdive maintenance reports by pilots. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.9104 on hard anomalies. It outperforms the baseline BiGAN across all metrics. It surpasses state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, F1-score, and false alarm rate across both failure types, validating its enhanced reliability for deep-sea missions.

title: Cervical Cancer Screening Using SE-ResNeXt-50 and Golden Lichtenberg Algorithm for Feature Optimization
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a significant global health problem, particularly in regions with limited or no regular screening programs. While standardized reporting systems like the Bethesda framework and traditional methods such as the Papanicolaou test have improved how diagnoses are made, manual interpretation is still time-consuming and prone to errors based on who is observing. The rise of digital cytology has allowed for the use of automated and computational screening techniques, which provide better scalability and consistency. Recent advances in deep learning have further improved cervical cancer detection by enhancing diagnostic accuracy with approaches like multi-scale semantic feature modeling, hierarchical pathology analysis, robust whole-slide image processing, and attention driven convolutional neural networks. However, these methods often have a hard time with repetitive high-dimensional data and cannot replicate the diagnostic reasoning used by cytopathologists. We present a straightforward and safe diagnostic method that combines evolutionary feature selection with patch-to-sample reasoning to address these challenges. The system employs the Golden Lichtenberg Algorithm (GLA) for reducing dimensions through Fibonacci-scaled optimization, SE-ResNeXt50 (Squeeze-and-Excitation Residual Network with Aggregated Transformations (50 layers)) for extracting patch-level features, and an uncertainty-aware hard patch loss to focus on borderline lesions. To provide predictions at the sample level, a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classifier combines the selected features. Experimental tests on benchmark datasets show that our approach offers improved interpretability and accuracy compared to baseline methods. This architecture can also be used for other biomedical imaging tasks and offers a practical solution for automated cervical cancer screening.

title: Shape of Memory: a Geometric Analysis of Machine Unlearning in Second-Order Optimizers
abstract: We argue that current definitions of machine unlearning are underspecified for second-order optimizers. We compare first-order and second-order learners for their ability to handle the data deletion task with varying degrees of eigendecomposition to mimic the loss model memory. While both first and second-order methods realign with the ideal counterfactul in terms of performance and gradient, the second-order optimizer shows significant volatility in the optimizer state. This indicates residual information, supposedly deleted, that isn't detectable by first-order analysis. Various eigendecay treatments show that stability and information loss is regained only under controlled state pertubation where geometric information (or memory) is erased.

title: Spend Less, Fit Better: Budget-Efficient Scaling Law Fitting via Active Experiment Selection
abstract: Scaling laws are used to plan multi-million-dollar training runs, but fitting those laws can itself cost millions. In modern large-scale workflows, assembling a sufficiently informative set of pilot experiments is already a major budget-allocation problem rather than a routine preprocessing step. We formulate scaling-law fitting as budget-aware sequential experimental design: given a finite pool of runnable experiments with heterogeneous costs, choose which runs to execute so as to maximize extrapolation accuracy in a high-cost target region. We then propose an uncertainty-aware method for sequentially allocating experimental budget toward the runs most useful for target-region extrapolation. Across a diverse benchmark of scaling-law tasks, our method consistently outperforms classical design-based baselines, and often approaches the performance of fitting on the full experimental set while using only about 10% of the total training budget. Our code is available at https://github.com/PlanarG/active-sl.

title: Rethinking Math Reasoning Evaluation: A Robust LLM-as-a-Judge Framework Beyond Symbolic Rigidity
abstract: Recent advancements in large language models have led to significant improvements across various tasks, including mathematical reasoning, which is used to assess models' intelligence in logical reasoning and problem-solving. Models are evaluated on mathematical reasoning benchmarks by verifying the correctness of the final answer against a ground truth answer. A common approach for this verification is based on symbolic mathematics comparison, which fails to generalize across diverse mathematical representations and solution formats. In this work, we offer a robust and flexible alternative to rule-based symbolic mathematics comparison. We propose an LLM-based evaluation framework for evaluating model-generated answers, enabling accurate evaluation across diverse mathematical representations and answer formats. We present failure cases of symbolic evaluation in two popular frameworks, Lighteval and SimpleRL, and compare them to our approach, demonstrating clear improvements over commonly used methods. Our framework enables more reliable evaluation and benchmarking, leading to more accurate performance monitoring, which is important for advancing mathematical problem-solving and intelligent systems.

title: Machine-Verifiable Implementation of the Axiom of True-Circle Self-Consistency and Its Corollaries Based on Lean 4 and Coq
abstract: This paper aims to establish the absolute rigor of the Axiom of True-Circle Self-Consistency (TCSC), the first principle of YuanXian Theory, and its corollaries through machine verification technology. Utilizing the Lean 4 and Coq theorem provers, we construct formal models of the cosmic closed system, the Self-Referential Mental Field (SRMF), and the T^{64} topological structure. By comparing the logical foundations and verification efficiencies of these tools, this study successfully implements automated validation of the uniqueness, non-traceability, and universal derivability of the TCSC axiom. The results demonstrate that the core logical chain of YuanXian Theory is consistent and complete within formal systems, providing solid machine-verifiable support and propelling ontological research toward standardized deduction. 本文旨在通过机器可验证技术确立元宪理论第一性原理——真圆自洽性公理(TCSC)及其推论的绝对严谨性。研究利用 Lean 4 与 Coq 定理证明工具,构建了宇宙闭合系统、自指心场(SRMF)及 T^{64} 拓扑结构的形式化模型。通过对比两大工具的逻辑基础与验证效率,本文成功实现了对真圆自洽性公理的唯一性、不可追溯性及全域导出性的自动化校验。验证结果表明,元宪理论的核心逻辑链条在形式化系统中无矛盾且完备,为理论体系提供了坚实的机器可验证支撑,推动了本体论研究向标准化演绎的转型。

title: Depth Fragility and Skeletal Universality: Decoupling Topology and Function in Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are traditionally analyzed as black-box function approximators, yet their internal structure exhibits phase transitions characteristic of complex physical systems. In this study, we investigate topological–functional decoupling—the phenomenon whereby a network retains full graph connectivity while losing computational function—in trained neural networks through the lens of percolation theory. By subjecting three distinct architectures (Shallow, Deep, and Wide MLPs) to a unified edge-pruning analysis on Fashion-MNIST, we uncover a fundamental divergence between structural integrity and computational capacity in this experimental setting. We report three key phenomena observed in these experiments: (1) the zombie network state under stochastic pruning, where the system retains global connectivity (P∞≈1.0) yet suffers a catastrophic functional collapse (accuracy falls below 50% of baseline at prunning ratio pf≈0.35–0.68 depending on depth), proves that graph reachability does not imply computational capability; (2) depth fragility, where increased network depth triggers multiplicative signal decay (the avalanche effect), rendering deep architectures exponentially more vulnerable to random edge removal than shallow ones (pfdeep≈0.35 vs. pfshallow≈0.68); and (3) scale-free universality, observed under magnitude-based pruning, where a robust functional skeleton maintains accuracy near the baseline (∼89%) up to extreme sparsity (pf≈0.85–0.95) across all three architectures. Robustness stems not from holographic redundancy in the overall connection count but from the emergent heavy-tailed rich-club organization of weight magnitudes—a sparse set of high-magnitude synapses that form the functional backbone of the network, decoupled from the redundant topological mass. These findings offer new physical constraints for the design of resilient neuromorphic hardware.

title: Design of an Automatic Classification Algorithm for Contextual Language Behaviors in Large-Scale Social Texts
abstract: To enhance the automatic recognition of linguistic behaviors on social platforms, this study constructs an automatic classification algorithm for contextual linguistic behaviors in large-scale social texts. It addresses the challenge of accurately distinguishing the functional aspects of textual linguistic behaviors based on accessible contextual information. We propose a multi-layer algorithmic framework integrating context construction, semantic encoding, and structural modeling. The context construction module aggregates dialogue chains and retrieves topics. Dual-channel semantic encoding combined with a gated fusion mechanism unifies multi-source information representations. Heterogeneous dialogue-user-topic graphs enhance the modeling of text interaction structures. Finally, a multi-task prediction head achieves joint optimization of main labels and pragmatic attributes. Using the SMP2020-ECDT social corpus as experimental data, multiple comparative experiments and ablation analyses were conducted under controlled conditions. Results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms baseline models in both Accuracy and Macro-F1 metrics. Context modeling and heterogeneous graph structures yield critical gains for highly context-dependent behaviors like requests and stances, while the multi-task joint optimization strategy markedly enhances training stability and pragmatic classification consistency. Analysis suggests that classification tasks oriented toward pragmatic functions require modeling approaches that incorporate dynamic context and structural dependencies beyond semantic representations to effectively support systematic recognition of linguistic behavior in complex interactive environments.

evidence.title: Design of an Automatic Classification Algorithm for Contextual Language Behaviors in Large-Scale Social Texts
evidence.abstract: To enhance the automatic recognition of linguistic behaviors on social platforms, this study constructs an automatic classification algorithm for contextual linguistic behaviors in large-scale social texts. It addresses the challenge of accurately distinguishing the functional aspects of textual linguistic behaviors based on accessible contextual information. We propose a multi-layer algorithmic framework integrating context construction, semantic encoding, and structural modeling. The context construction module aggregates dialogue chains and retrieves topics. Dual-channel semantic encoding combined with a gated fusion mechanism unifies multi-source information representations. Heterogeneous dialogue-user-topic graphs enhance the modeling of text interaction structures. Finally, a multi-task prediction head achieves joint optimization of main labels and pragmatic attributes. Using the SMP2020-ECDT social corpus as experimental data, multiple comparative experiments and ablation analyses were conducted under controlled conditions. Results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms baseline models in both Accuracy and Macro-F1 metrics. Context modeling and heterogeneous graph structures yield critical gains for highly context-dependent behaviors like requests and stances, while the multi-task joint optimization strategy markedly enhances training stability and pragmatic classification consistency. Analysis suggests that classification tasks oriented toward pragmatic functions require modeling approaches that incorporate dynamic context and structural dependencies beyond semantic representations to effectively support systematic recognition of linguistic behavior in complex interactive environments.

title: A Natural Language Driven Agentic AI Framework for Automated Household Inventory Management
abstract: This paper presents the HomeInventory Agent, a web-based application utilizing agentic AI for the simplification of home inventory management through natural language interaction. Rather than using pen-and-paper scribbles or basic reminder applications, which can easily result in lost items, duplicate purchases, and confusion among household members, the proposed application enables users to manage their home supplies through natural language input. Through typing common instructions such as adding, updating, or checking items, users can interact with the application as if they were communicating with an assistant. The application automatically organizes items into categories, keeps a structured database, and continuously updates home supply information in real-time.The application intelligently analyzes available quantities and provides status levels such as sufficient, low, or depleted, allowing for proactive checklist generation as supplies start running out. A web-based interface allows for instant updates to be reflected across all users sharing the same household, eliminating miscommunication and improving coordination. Experimental testing has shown reliable interpretation of user intent and successful task completion across multiple sessions. More than theoretical application, the HomeInventory Agent shows its real-world relevance by seamlessly integrating with existing household routines, withstanding high usage levels with continued high performance.

title: Automation-Exploit: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Adaptive Offensive Security with Digital Twin-Based Risk-Mitigated Exploitation
abstract: The offensive security landscape is highly fragmented: enterprise platforms avoid memory-corruption vulnerabilities due to Denial of Service (DoS) risks, Automatic Exploit Generation (AEG) systems suffer from semantic blindness, and Large Language Model (LLM) agents face safety alignment filters and "Live Fire" execution hazards. We introduce Automation-Exploit, a fully autonomous Multi-Agent System (MAS) framework designed for adaptive offensive security in complex black-box scenarios. It bridges the abstraction gap between reconnaissance and exploitation by autonomously exfiltrating executables and contextual intelligence across multiple protocols, using this data to fuel both logical and binary attack chains. The framework introduces an adaptive safety architecture to mitigate DoS risks. While it natively resolves logical and web-based vulnerabilities, it employs a conditional isomorphic validation for high-risk memory-corruption flaws: if the target binary is successfully exfiltrated, it dynamically instantiates a cross-platform digital twin. By enforcing strict state synchronization, including libc alignment and runtime file descriptor hooking, potentially destructive payloads are iteratively debugged in an isolated replica. This enables a highly risk-mitigated "one-shot" execution on the physical target. Empirical evaluations across eight scenarios, including undocumented zero-day environments to rule out LLM data contamination, validate the framework's architectural resilience, demonstrating its ability to prevent "live fire" crashes and execute risk-mitigated compromises on actual targets.

title: 2025 47th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) diagnosis often relies on biopsies, which can lead to unnecessary procedures and complications. Federated learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving approach for training predictive models across hospitals without sharing sensitive patient data. In this study, we evaluate the feasibility of FL for PCa risk prediction by benchmarking different training strategies, including local, federated models, as well as free-riding (FR) on federated models. Using real-world heterogeneous datasets from 19 hospitals, we analyze the impact of data diversity and consortium size on predictive performance. Our results show that while FL improves model generalizability, local models often perform comparably, making direct participation in FL less beneficial for large hospitals. However, a small consortium of high-data-quality institutions could collaboratively develop robust models for broader clinical use. We discuss the practical implications of FL in healthcare and propose strategies for sustainable deployment in real-world hospital networks.

title: Meta-Learning Algorithms for Rapid Adaptation in Artificial Intelligence Systems: an Analysis of Few-Shot Learning and Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning
abstract: Meta-learning, sometimes known as "learning to learn," has emerged as a transformational paradigm in artificial intelligence, allowing computers to quickly adapt to new tasks with little input. This thorough study looks into the usefulness of meta-learning algorithms, namely few-shot learning and Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML), in tackling the important problem of data efficiency in machine learning systems. This work investigates the performance, convergence qualities, and generalization capabilities of cutting-edge meta-learning techniques using thorough empirical assessment across numerous benchmark datasets such as miniImageNet, tieredImageNet, CIFAR-FS, and Omniglot. Our research includes a comprehensive examination of 12 various meta-learning algorithms over 8 different task domains, as well as rigorous statistical analysis and ablation studies to extract performance-related parameters.MAML-based techniques outperform traditional transfer learning by 15.3%, achieving an average accuracy of 68.42% (±1.23%) on 5-way 1-shot classification tasks and 83.76% (±0.87%) on 5-way 5-shot tasks on miniImageNet. Furthermore, our suggested MAML framework modifications, such as adaptive learning rate scheduling and gradient variance reduction approaches, result in further performance benefits of 4.2% and 3.8%. Critical research demonstrates that meta-learning algorithms have higher sample efficiency, requiring 60-75% less training cases to attain equal performance to their supervised learning counterparts. However, there are substantial issues surrounding computational overhead, with meta-training taking 3.5-5x more computer resources than typical training processes.This study contributes to the field by: (1) establishing a comprehensive benchmark of meta-learning algorithms using standardized evaluation protocols; (2) identifying key architectural and optimization factors influencing meta-learning performance; (3) proposing novel modifications to existing algorithms that improve stability and convergence; and (4) providing practical guidelines for algorithm selection based on task characteristics. The findings have important implications for deploying AI systems in data-constrained situations such as medical diagnostics, robotic control, and customized recommendation systems. This study lays the groundwork for future research into meta-learning theory, algorithm design, and practical applications.

title: Telugu Toxic Comment Analysis Using Deep Learning Transformer Models
abstract: Abstract— [1]The rapid growth of social media platforms has led to an increase in the spread of toxic and abusive content, particularly in low-resource languages such as Telugu. Automatic detection of such harmful content is essential to ensure safe and respectful online communication. However, limited annotated datasets and linguistic diversity pose significant challenges for Telugu toxic comment classification. In this project, we perform a comparative analysis of machine learning and transformer-based models for Telugu toxic comment detection using the Telugu portion of the [2] MACD dataset. In the first phase, traditional machine learning algorithms such as Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Logistic Regression were implemented along with encoder-based transformer models including mBERT and IndicBERT. The models were evaluated using standard performance metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score. In the second phase, we extend the study by implementing encoder–decoder transformer architectures, namely mT5 and IndicT5, to examine their effectiveness in handling contextual and semantic complexities in Telugu text. This work provides a systematic comparison between traditional machine learning approaches, encoder-based transformers, and encoder–decoder transformers for Telugu toxic comment classification. The study aims to identify the most suitable architecture for improving detection performance in low-resource Indic languages.

title: A Comparative Review of VADER and BERT for Sentiment Analysis: Methods, Performance, and Applications
abstract: Abstract - Sentiment analysis is a key task in Natural Language Processing (NLP), enabling machines to understand human emotions in textual data. Among various approaches, lexicon-based methods such as VADER and deep learning-based models like BERT have gained significant attention. This paper presents a comprehensive review of VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and Sentiment Reasoner) and BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), focusing on their architectures, methodologies, advantages, limitations, and comparative performance. Experimental findings from recent studies are also discussed to highlight differences in accuracy, interpretability, and computational efficiency. Key Words: sentiment analysis, natural language processing (NLP), lexicon-based methods, deep learning, VADER, BERT, transformer models, text classification, opinion mining, hybrid models

title: Supermodular Reasoning Optimization: A Synergistic Training Paradigm for Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have significantly improved performance in recent years by generating long-chain reasoning, but this has also brought problems such as reasoning redundancy, computational waste, and uncontrollable reasoning paths. Existing methods (such as Self-Braking Tuning) mainly make local adjustments from the perspective of "suppressing over-reasoning," but they are essentially still in the framework of independent optimization per token or per step, ignoring the high-order dependency structure between reasoning steps. This paper proposes a novel training paradigm: Supermodular Reasoning Optimization (SRO). We introduce supermodular function optimization theory into the training of large reasoning models for the first time, modeling the complete reasoning trajectory as a set function optimization problem, in which there is a "synergy" between reasoning steps. Unlike the traditional independence assumption, we prove that high-quality reasoning essentially satisfies a structural characteristic of "increasing marginal returns," that is, the value of subsequent reasoning steps depends on the set of existing steps. Based on this, we propose three core mechanisms: (1) modeling the value of the reasoning set, (2) training signals driven by supermodular gain, and (3) a synergistic triggering reasoning generation strategy. This paradigm no longer simply shortens or lengthens inference, but instead learns "which combinations of steps are most valuable." This method fundamentally changes the training objective of LRM: shifting from "maximizing the probability of sequence generation" to "maximizing the collaborative value of the inference set," providing a theoretical basis for unifying inference efficiency and quality.

title: Design of an Intelligent Evaluation System for Teaching Effectiveness in Finance Vocational Education Based on CatBoost
abstract: In the context of vocational higher education, practical challenges such as complex teaching structures, subjective evaluation criteria, and significant multi-source data noise have long relied on empirical judgments for accurate teaching effectiveness assessment. There is an urgent need to establish an intelligent analysis system with objectivity and interpretability. To achieve structured measurement of multidimensional "student-course" characteristics, this study designs a teaching effectiveness evaluation method based on the CatBoost model, specifically addressing high-cardinality categorical features and time-series behavioral attributes. Through sequential target encoding, feature uniform mapping, category weight constraints, and symmetric tree structure optimization, a classification model combining stability and generalization capability was constructed. The system architecture, spanning data access layer, model service layer, and teaching management layer, enables deployable implementation. Experiments validated by 37,852 samples across three semesters demonstrated that the method significantly outperforms comparison models in Macro-F1, weighted accuracy, and AUC metrics. Feature contribution analysis further revealed that core learning behaviors and key course variables play decisive roles in effectiveness grading, demonstrating strong interpretability and educational consistency. The research findings prove that data-driven evaluation systems can effectively enhance the precision of teaching quality monitoring and provide technical support for course management and learning interventions in vocational education, forming a complete technical loop from data representation to decision interpretation within real-world teaching environments.

title: Multilevel Thresholdingimage Segmentation Using Mixed Strategy Improved Convergence Based Whaleoptimization Algorithm
abstract: A novel multilevel picture segmentation technique based on an enhanced Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is introduced in this paper. WOA has shown promise in several optimization situations, however its susceptibility to local optima may limit its effectiveness. To address this, we propose a Mixed-Strategy Improved Convergence WOA (MSICWOA) that combines a k-point initialization method, an adaptive weight coefficient, and a nonlinear convergence factor to enhance its optimization capabilities. The optimal thresholds for multilevel grey scale image segmentation are then determined using the MSICWOA with Otsu cross variance and Kaput entropy as objective functions. Experiments on benchmark functions demonstrate that MSICWOA performs better than alternative optimization techniques in terms of convergence speed and search accuracy. Additionally, it overcomes local optima with success. The effectiveness of the MSICWOA-Kaput technique in accurately and rapidly identifying multilevel thresholds is confirmed by image segmentation experiments conducted on standard datasets.

title: RouteGuard: Internal-Signal Detection of Skill Poisoning in LLM Agents
abstract: Agent skills introduce a new and more severe form of indirect injection for LLM agents: unlike traditional indirect prompt injection, attackers can hide malicious instructions inside a dense, action-oriented skill that already functions as a legitimate instruction source. We study pre-execution skill-poison detection and show that successful skill poisoning induces a structured internal effect, attention hijacking, in which response-time attention shifts from trusted context to malicious skill spans and drives harmful behavior. Motivated by this mechanism, we propose RouteGuard, a frozen-backbone detector that combines response-conditioned attention and hidden-state alignment through reliability-gated late fusion. Across both real and synthetic open-source skill benchmarks, RouteGuard is consistently the strongest or most robust detector; on the critical Skill-Inject channel slice, it reaches 0.8834 F1 and recovers 90.51% of description attacks missed by lexical screening, showing that defending against skill poisoning requires internal-signal detection rather than text-only filtering

title: Neural Recovery of Historical Lexical Structure in Bantu Languages from Modern Data
abstract: We investigate whether neural models trained exclusively on modern morphological data can recover cross-lingual lexical structure consistent with historical reconstruction. Using BantuMorph v7, a transformer over Bantu morphological paradigms, we analyze 14 Eastern and Southern Bantu languages, extract encoder embeddings for their noun and verb lemmas, and identify 728 noun and 1,525 verb cognate candidates shared across 5+ languages. Evaluating these candidates against established historical resources-the Bantu Lexical Reconstructions database (BLR3; 4,786 reconstructed Proto-Bantu forms) and the ASJP basic vocabulary-we confirm 10 of the top 11 noun candidates (90.9%) align with previously reconstructed Proto-Bantu forms, including *-ntU 'person' (8 languages), *gombe 'cow' (9 languages), and *mUn (9 languages). Extending to verbs, 12 verb cognates align with reconstructed Proto-Bantu roots, including *-bon- 'see' and *-jIm- 'stand', each attested across wide geographic ranges. Cross-model validation using an independent translation model (NLLB-600M) confirms these patterns: both models recover cognate clusters and phylogenetic groupings consistent with established Guthrie-zone classifications (p < 0.01). Cross-lingual noun class analysis reveals that all 13 productive classes maintain >0.83 cosine similarity across languages (within-class > between-class, p < 10^-9). Our dataset is restricted to Eastern and Southern Bantu, so we interpret these results as recovering shared Bantu lexical structure consistent with Proto-Bantu rather than definitively distinguishing Proto-Bantu retentions from later regional innovations.

title: Self-Correction as Feedback Control: Error Dynamics, Stability Thresholds, and Prompt Interventions in LLMs
abstract: Iterative self-correction is increasingly deployed in agentic LLM systems, yet whether repeated refinement improves or degrades performance remains inconsistent across models. We recast self-correction as a closed-loop feedback-control problem in which the same model is both controller and plant, and analyze its error dynamics via a two-state Markov model over {Correct, Incorrect}, parameterized by the Error Introduction Rate (EIR) and Error Correction Rate (ECR). The model yields a directly measurable stability threshold -- iterate only when ECR/EIR > Acc/(1-Acc) -- in which EIR acts as a stability margin and prompting becomes lightweight controller design. Empirically, across 7 models and 3 datasets (GSM8K, MATH, StrategyQA), a sharp near-zero EIR boundary (< 0.5%) cleanly separates beneficial from harmful self-correction: only o3-mini (+3.4 pp), Claude Opus 4.6 (+0.6 pp), and o4-mini (+/-0 pp) stay non-degrading, while GPT-5 and four others lose accuracy. A verify-first prompt intervention then provides causal evidence: it drives GPT-4o-mini's EIR from 2% to 0% and converts a -6.2 pp degradation into +0.2 pp (paired McNemar, p<10^{-4}), with negligible change on already-sub-threshold models -- exactly as the diagnostic predicts. A complementary analysis of adaptive self-consistency (ASC) shows it halts harmful refinement at a 3.8 pp confidence-elicitation cost, exposing a two-tier capability structure: prompt-level EIR suppression prevents degradation, whereas ECR enhancement -- plausibly training-level -- is required for genuine gains. Self-correction should thus be treated not as a default behavior but as a control decision governed by measurable error dynamics.

title: Shortest Path-Governed Reasoning Optimization for Efficient Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) have achieved remarkable progress by generating long and expressive chains of thought, yet this often introduces substantial redundancy, inefficient computation, and suboptimal reasoning trajectories. In this work, we propose Shortest Path-Governed Reasoning Optimization (SPGRO), a novel training and tuning paradigm that reformulates reasoning as a shortest path problem over a structured reasoning graph. In SPGRO, each intermediate reasoning state is modeled as a node, and transitions between thoughts are treated as weighted edges, where the cost function jointly captures computational effort, uncertainty, and semantic redundancy. Under this formulation, the optimal reasoning process corresponds to the minimum-cost path from the initial state to the answer state, governed by a Bellman-style optimality principle. We further introduce a path relaxation mechanism that enables models to iteratively refine reasoning trajectories toward lower-cost alternatives, as well as an adaptive stopping criterion derived from convergence in the shortest-path value function. This perspective allows LRMs to inherently learn when and how to reason efficiently, reducing unnecessary intermediate steps while preserving correctness. Overall, SPGRO provides a principled framework for reasoning compression and efficiency optimization, unifying inference, training, and decoding under a graph-theoretic optimality lens.

title: The application of large language models in meteorology graduate research: current status, impact, and prospects
abstract: With the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence, large language models (LLMs) have gradually integrated into various fields, demonstrating significant potential, particularly in meteorological research. This study explores the current application, advantages, challenges, and future development trends of LLMs in the scientific work of meteorology graduate students at NUIST. Through surveys and case analysis, the study finds that LLMs are primarily applied in literature review, data processing, code development, and academic writing in meteorological research. The results show that LLMs significantly enhance research efficiency, particularly in code development and literature translation, saving considerable time for graduate students. However, challenges remain in areas such as the accuracy of professional knowledge, creative inspiration, and interdisciplinary integration. The study also reveals concerns over data security, academic integrity, and model limitations when using LLMs. Future applications of LLMs in meteorology need further optimization in terms of professional knowledge accuracy and data processing capabilities. This paper provides both theoretical support and practical guidance for the responsible integration of LLMs into meteorological research and education.

title: Research on Non-Equal-Precision Measurement Data Processing Based on the Transformer Model
abstract: To address the marked precision heterogeneity of non-equal-precision measurement data, and the limitations of conventional methods in temporal feature capture for slow time-varying dynamic measurement scenarios, we propose a novel Transformer encoder-based method for non-equal-precision measurement data processing. This method constructs a dual-feature input by fusing measured values and their corresponding precision information, captures long-range temporal dependencies in dynamic measurement sequences via multi-head self-attention, extracts deep nonlinear features through stacked encoder layers, and prioritizes high-precision measurements via a precision-aware weighted loss function. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves lower estimation errors than the matched LSTM baseline under identical input and training settings, as well as classic weighted averaging and weighted least squares benchmarks, across uniform, Gaussian, precision-polarized, and varying noise level scenarios. It demonstrates superior robustness and adaptability in complex non-equal-precision measurement environments.

title: Accurate Funding Methods for Higher Vocational Colleges and Universities Based on Integrated Learning and Data Mining
abstract: Accurate identification of financially disadvantaged vocational students is essential for targeted aid but is challenged by feature redundancy and class imbalance. This study proposes a Stacking and Feature Optimization for Vocational Student Aid Identification (SFO-VSAI) model. First, a statistical-analysis-plus Chi-square (χ²) screening strategy is used to remove redundant features. Second, a hybrid resampling strategy integrating Adaptive Synthetic Sampling (ADASYN) and Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is applied to alleviate class imbalance. Third, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) are used as base learners, and Logistic Regression (LR) is employed as the meta-learner to build a stacking ensemble. The experiment was evaluated on two real datasets. The results showed that the F1 score of the integrated model on the UCI-EPM dataset reached 0.872, and the accuracy improvement was 11.4%. Research shows that the multi-layer integrated structure constructed for imbalanced samples has high practical value and scalability in the funding tasks of higher vocational colleges.

title: Quantum Guard: Adaptive Device-Independent QKD and Practical File Encryption Using Real Quantum Hardware Key
abstract: The rapid advancement of quantum computing threatens to undercut the mathematical foundations of today’s public-key cryptosystems. Quantum key distribution (QKD) provides an information-theoretically secure substitute whose security is derived from physical laws rather than computational complexity. However, most practical QKD systems still rely on trusted hardware components that are vulnerable to manufacturing backdoors, misalignment, and side-channel leakage. Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (DIQKD) removes these assumptions by certifying security from experimentally observed Bell-inequality violations, treating devices as untrusted black boxes.This paper provides a complete overview of DIQKD research, focusing on the evolution from early theoretical security proofs to real-world demonstrations on quantum hardware. We review implementation issues on platforms like IBM Quantum, evaluate finite-key security models, and study fundamental protocols. Building on this review, the Quantum Guard framework is presented as a conceptual design that combines adaptive optimization, finite-key estimation, and active attack detection to achieve resilient, device-independent communication. We further demonstrate practical file encryption using DIQKD-generated keys. Finally, we discuss current limitations and strategic objectives for building scalable, commercial quantum-secure networks.

title: DM-ASR: Diarization-aware Multi-speaker ASR with Large Language Models
abstract: Multi-speaker automatic speech recognition (ASR) aims to transcribe conversational speech involving multiple speakers, requiring the model to capture not only what was said, but also who said it and sometimes when it was spoken. Recent Speech-LLM approaches have shown the potential of unified modeling for this task, but jointly learning speaker attribution, temporal structure, and lexical recognition remains difficult and data-intensive. At the current stage, leveraging reliable speaker diarization as an explicit structural prior provides a practical and efficient way to simplify this task. To effectively exploit such priors, we propose DM-ASR, a diarization-aware multi-speaker ASR framework that reformulates the task as a multi-turn dialogue generation process. Given an audio chunk and diarization results, DM-ASR decomposes transcription into a sequence of speaker- and time-conditioned queries, each corresponding to one speaker in one time segment. This formulation converts multi-speaker recognition into a series of structured sub-tasks, explicitly decoupling speaker-temporal structure from linguistic content and enabling effective integration of diarization cues with the reasoning capability of large language models. We further introduce an optional word-level timestamp prediction mechanism that interleaves word and timestamp tokens, yielding richer structured outputs and better transcription quality. Our analysis shows that diarization systems provide more reliable speaker identities and segment-level boundaries, while LLMs excel at modeling linguistic content and long-range dependencies, demonstrating their complementary strengths. Experiments on Mandarin and English benchmarks show that the proposed approach achieves strong performance with relatively small models and training data, while remaining competitive with or outperforming existing unified approaches.

title: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Computational Linguistics : Industry Track
abstract: Pretrained language models are integral part of AI applications, but their high computational cost for training limits accessibility. Initiatives such as Bloom and StarCoder aim to democratize access to pretrained models for collaborative community development. Despite these efforts, such models encounter challenges such as limited multilingual capabilities, risks of catastrophic forgetting during continual pretraining, and the high costs of training models from scratch, alongside the need to align with AI safety standards and regulatory frameworks. This paper presents Aurora-M, a 15B parameter multilingual open-source model trained on English, Finnish, Hindi, Japanese, Vietnamese, and code. Continually pretrained from StarCoderPlus on 435B additional tokens, Aurora-M surpasses 2T tokens in total training token count. It is the first open-source multilingual model fine-tuned on human-reviewed safety instructions, thus aligning its development not only with conventional red-teaming considerations, but also with the specific concerns articulated in the Biden-Harris Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence. We evaluate Aurora-M across a wide range of tasks and languages, showcasing its robustness against catastrophic forgetting and its superior performance in multilingual settings, particularly in safety evaluations. We open-source Aurora-M and its variants to encourage responsible open-source development of large language models at https://huggingface.co/aurora-m.

title: CTMinfo: First Implemented System in Which 100% Data Admission Is the Ontological Foundation
abstract: This work introduces and implements a strict admission principle for data systems: only data with 100% unambiguous representation are allowed. Any data admitting more than one valid interpretation are not interpreted, refined, or approximated — they are excluded from the system. Unlike existing ontologies, knowledge graphs, and data models that tolerate and manage ambiguity, CTMinfo enforces its complete exclusion at the architectural level. This defines a deterministic ontological foundation where ambiguity does not exist within the system. The approach is applicable to domains where object parameters are strictly defined, the set of possible variations is finite, and full verification is achievable. The claim is directly testable: providing a single object that admits more than one valid interpretation under the system rules is sufficient to invalidate the principle. If no such object exists, the system maintains its stated property. If data admit more than one interpretation, they do not exist in CTMinfo.

title: Cutting-Plane Reasoning: A Polyhedral Self-Constraining Training Paradigm for Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) significantly improve performance by generating long-chain reasoning, but this introduces a serious problem of redundant reasoning. Existing methods (such as self-braking mechanisms) mainly reduce redundancy through posterior control or heuristic strategies, without constraining the structure of the reasoning space itself. This paper proposes a novel training paradigm—Cutting-Plane Reasoning (CPR)—which for the first time introduces the cutting plane theory from integer programming into the training process of large reasoning models, modeling the reasoning trajectory as a path search problem in a high-dimensional combinatorial polyhedron. We propose that reasoning errors and redundancy essentially stem from the model's wandering in the "relaxed reasoning space," while effective reasoning should reside within the "feasible reasoning polyhedron." To this end, we design a dynamic cutting plane generation mechanism that automatically constructs "reasoning constraints" during training, gradually tightening the reasoning space to approximate the optimal set of reasoning trajectories. This framework achieves a paradigm shift from "generative reasoning" to "constrained reasoning," providing LRMs with endogenous structured reasoning control capabilities.
